name: browser-readonly-catalog
description:
A readonly browser toolbox's recorded tool catalog is the claim: web_navigate, web_read and web_find are offered, web_click and web_type are not, and a navigate+read round trip actually reaches the fixture's own test site and returns its content.

Two user turns, a plain warm-up then the real ask. The original sketch assumed the browser refresher only synthesizes a toolbox's tools onto the live set on the turn AFTER MarkBrowserReady stamps status.resolvedBrowserToolboxes (mirroring the secret-gated sidecar's slower, Secret-propagation-gated arrival). Measured directly instead (three consecutive standalone runs): markBrowserFixtureReady's status patch — fired right after the first, fire-and-forget SendUserMessage returns — consistently lands before the runner's first mid-session tool-refresh check, so the tools are already present on turn 1's own first LLM request. This bundle does not assert toolNotOffered on turn 1 for that reason (an earlier draft did and failed consistently against the real driver); the warm-up/real-ask split is kept for readability, not as a timing proof.

toolOffered/toolNotOffered are spread across turn 2's three requests (one offered- and one not-offered-check per step) rather than all piled on the first, because Expect carries exactly one of each per step — the three offered names (web_navigate, web_read, web_find) and the spec's "a tool not offered cannot be called" are still each checked once. web_click/web_type do not exist as ops at all in Phase A (pkg/agent/tool/browser/synthesize.go offers the identical observation set regardless of interaction), so those two assertions pass today independent of readonly — they are the standing guard for Phase C's acting tools, exactly as the brief says.

lastToolResultContains on both the navigate result ("loaded") and the read result (the site's BRONZE-FARES-TABLE sentinel) is what proves the round trip actually reached the fixture site and read its real content back, rather than a scripted reply standing in for it.
userTurns: please check the fares page at http://{{browserSite}}/ and tell me what's listed

reply.text: Hello! How can I help you today?
The fares page shows BRONZE-FARES-TABLE: NYC-LAX $199.
